report:
Fresh final followup review of index_namespace_pages. Saved/read the previous report and inputs, started fresh, recaptured all four dependencies and compared every fragment. The initial claim, whole anchors.rs and complete integration test are unchanged. The only dependency delta is an implementation_references association comment in spec.rs; fixture helpers, book entry and review machinery are unchanged. No generation or namespace behavior changed.

The full claim requires all active rules on the landing, restricted tables for every prefix, direct canonical-name routes, surrounding namespace navigation, combined own-claim/descendants pages for prefix rules, and no new definitions from generated pages. The sole ordinary generate association consumes spec.anchors. names with empty prefix yields all rules; within uses equality or dot-delimited descent. children deduplicates immediate namespace components and recursively creates their pages. anchor_url maps dotted names to design/anchor/name/components.html, with corresponding mdBook paths. Each generated chapter has null source_path. page renders its own definition/context when its prefix is a rule, supplies its descendants table when applicable, and renders surrounding namespace navigation and breadcrumbs. Pure namespace pages use the same restricted table builder. Generation does not mutate the canonical index; spec excludes generated design/anchor content from normative definitions. The new comment does not affect any of these operations.

The complete ordinary generated_anchor_pages_join_namespaces_claims_implementations_tests_and_reviews test constructs meta.foo, meta.foo.bar and meta.other.leaf and invokes the real preprocessor. It asserts exact landing rows for all three, existence of meta/meta.foo/meta.other prefix pages and a direct sibling leaf page, exact parent/sibling restricted row lists, one child under the rule-plus-prefix meta.foo, null source_path, and exact parent+child rows on its page. It checks canonical context and specification return links and requires a reloaded inventory of exactly three definitions. Additional formatting, excerpt, status and review assertions ensure actual populated pages, but the hierarchy assertions themselves establish this claim. Fixture/chapters helpers use real files/process output and reject duplicate paths; review helpers construct the fixture state through actual review APIs. Placeholder statuses in fixture data are not TODO evidence for this anchor.

There are no TODO/N/A associations or deferred requirements. All aspects of the prior complete assessment remain supported after checking the actual one-comment dependency delta and unchanged current tests. No source edits, build or behavior tests occurred; fresh review commands and source inspection only. No requested edits.
